title: AVM-BTB: Adaptive and Virtualized Multi-level Branch Target Buffer
problem: Branch Target Buffer capacity critically impacts prediction accuracy, but expanding BTB requires valuable on-chip SRAM with prohibitive timing and area costs. Fixed-size BTBs waste power and resources because applications have varying BTB demands across different execution phases.
motivation: Efficient branch prediction is essential for processor performance, but current designs fail to adapt to varying application requirements, limiting speedup and wasting power.
method: AVM-BTB dynamically borrows cache capacity from Uop Cache and ICache as temporary BTB when branch prediction demands are high, returning capacity when not needed. A monitoring mechanism tracks BTB error rates and effective accesses to balance instruction data and prediction metadata, while Fetch Directed Instruction Prefetching compensates for reduced cache capacity.
key_novelty: Dynamic virtualization of cache capacity as temporary BTB, enabling adaptive resource reallocation between instruction caches and branch prediction storage based on runtime monitoring.
contributions: Empirically demonstrated that BTB requirements vary significantly across applications and execution stages
Proposed virtualized multi-level BTB architecture that borrows cache capacity without requiring additional SRAM
Developed runtime monitoring mechanism using BTB error rate and effective accesses to balance data and metadata
Achieved 18.22% average performance improvement with 2.77% power reduction across frontend-bound and frontend-friendly scenarios
limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract; does not detail boundary conditions where virtualization may not be effective.
primary_theme: Adaptive cache virtualization for branch prediction
